findings.title: Scaling and SMOTE applied to the full dataset before the train/test split
findings.quote: To handle class imbalance, SMOTE was applied to the full dataset before splitting.
findings.why_it_matters: Synthetic samples are interpolated from test records and min-max ranges include test values, so information from the test set leaks into training and the 96.4% accuracy is likely inflated.
findings.suggested_fix: Split first; fit imputation, scaling and SMOTE on the training data only (inside each cross-validation fold) and re-report all results.

findings.title: Hyperparameters selected on the test set
findings.quote: The number of epochs and the learning rate were selected based on the accuracy obtained on the test set.
findings.why_it_matters: Using the test set for tuning makes it part of model development, so the reported test accuracy is no longer an unbiased estimate of performance on new patients.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a separate validation split or nested cross-validation for tuning and keep the test set untouched until the final evaluation.

findings.title: Causal claim from a predictive model
findings.quote: Our results show that high glucose levels cause diabetes onset, and the model generalizes to any hospital population.
findings.why_it_matters: A classifier trained on observational records shows association, not causation, and one dataset from a single population cannot show generalisation to any hospital.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase as an association and limit the generalisation claim to the studied dataset, or add external validation on data from other hospitals.

findings.title: Deployment claim without external validation or limitations
findings.quote: The proposed approach can be directly deployed in hospitals.
findings.why_it_matters: Clinical deployment needs evidence from independent data and a discussion of limitations; the paper has neither.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or soften the deployment claim and add a limitations section (single small dataset, no external validation).
